title: Detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae by Real-Time PCR with the ZKIR System
author: Elodie Barbier
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7n6hmhe

steps.title: Prepare PCR controls
steps.instruction: Add PCR‑grade water as the negative control and dilute K. pneumoniae ATCC13883T DNA to 2 ng/µL to serve as the positive control.

steps.title: Establish melt‑curve reference
steps.instruction: Run the ZKIR assay on serial dilutions of K. pneumoniae ATCC13883T and record the melt‑curve peak, which occurs at approximately 80.2 °C.

steps.title: Enrich soil samples
steps.instruction: Combine 10 g of soil with 90 mL Lysogeny Broth (per litre: 5 g yeast extract, 5 g NaCl, 10 g tryptone) supplemented with ampicillin 10 mg/L; incubate 24 h at 30 °C.

steps.title: Enrich food samples
steps.instruction: Combine 25 g of food (e.g., salad or chicken) with 225 mL Buffered Peptone Water; incubate 24 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Centrifuge and wash enrichment
steps.instruction: Transfer 500 µL of each enrichment to a tube, centrifuge 5 min at 5,800 g, wash the pellet twice with sterile water, then boil the suspension for 10 min.

steps.title: Dilute boiled extracts
steps.instruction: Prepare undiluted (crude) extract and dilute the boiled suspension 1:10 and 1:100 with sterile water for downstream qPCR.

steps.title: Run ZKIR real‑time PCR
steps.instruction: Test the crude, 1:10‑diluted, and 1:100‑diluted DNA extracts together with the positive and negative controls using the ZKIR assay according to the kit protocol.
